title: Relative principal parts in etale polynomial coordinates
statement:
Let $R_0$ be a commutative ring, $n,t\ge0$, $S=R_0[z_1,\ldots,z_n]$, and $S\to R$ a homomorphism such that $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is etale [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put $\mathcal D=\ker(R\otimes_{R_0}R\to R)$ and $P^t_{R/R_0}=(R\otimes_{R_0}R)/\mathcal D^{t+1}$, with the first-factor $R$-algebra structure [def-trf-diagonal-jets]. There is a canonical $R$-algebra isomorphism
$$R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]/(Y)^{t+1}\simeq P^t_{R/R_0},\qquad Y_j\longmapsto 1\otimes z_j-z_j\otimes1.$$
Let $T_t:R\to R[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$ be $h\mapsto1\otimes h$ under its inverse; thus $T_t(z_j)=z_j+Y_j$ and $T_t(h)\bmod(Y)=h$. These isomorphisms are compatible with truncation in $t$. For every ring map $R_0\to R'_0$, set $R'=R\otimes_{R_0}R'_0$. The canonical map $P^t_{R/R_0}\otimes_{R_0}R'_0\to P^t_{R'/R'_0}$ is an isomorphism and identifies the displayed coordinate bases and the maps $T_t$ after base change [def-weil-module-base-change]. If $C$ is any commutative $R_0$-algebra and $\tau:R\to C[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$ is an $R_0$-algebra homomorphism with $\tau(z_j)=Z_j$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], applying $\tau$ to the coefficients of $T_t(h)$ gives
$$\tau(h)(Z+Y)\bmod(Y)^{t+1}\in C[[Z]][Y]/(Y)^{t+1}.$$
Here the right side is the continuous formal translation fixing $C$, defined coefficientwise by binomial expansion; no field, flatness, characteristic, ideal, supported basis, diagram or minor-ideal hypothesis is required. The assertions include $n=0$, $t=0$ and zero rings.

source.place: Tag 0H93 (lemma-formally-etale-omega), the diagonal-power quotient isomorphism, not only its final differential assertion; Tag 0H90 (lemma-principal-parts-diagonal); Tag 0H8Z (lemma-principal-parts-base-change). Polynomial diagonal calculation and compatibility with formal translation by the unique infinitesimal etale lift.

proof.text: Put $A=R\otimes_{R_0}S$ and $B=R\otimes_{R_0}R$, with multiplication of pure tensors factorwise. The polynomial and tensor universal properties identify $A$ with $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$: $r\otimes f(z)$ maps to $r f(X)$ and the inverse sends $r$ to $r\otimes1$ and $X_j$ to $1\otimes z_j$. The augmentation $e:A\to R$, $r\otimes s\mapsto rs$, is evaluation at $X_j=z_j$. The mutually inverse polynomial substitutions $Y_j=X_j-z_j$ and $X_j=Y_j+z_j$ identify $\ker e$ with $(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)$. Indeed evaluation at $Y=0$ kills exactly the polynomials with zero constant coefficient, each a sum of multiples of the $Y_j$. Consequently $A/(\ker e)^{t+1}=R[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$, freely spanned over $R$ by the monomials $Y^\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le t$: the discarded ideal consists exactly of sums of monomials of degree at least $t+1$.

source.place: Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega, polynomial case of its diagonal quotient; explicit polynomial substitutions.

proof.text: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ send $r\otimes s$ to $r\otimes s|_R$. It is the base change of $S\to R$ along $S\to A$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$: the identification $A\otimes_SR\simeq B$ sends $(r\otimes s)\otimes u$ to $r\otimes su$, with inverse $r\otimes u\mapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes u$. Both formulas respect the balancing relations and their composites fix pure tensors, which generate the tensor modules. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] with base ring $S$, etale algebra $R$, and new base algebra $A$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale; there is no finiteness or flatness assumption on $R_0$.

source.place: Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega, proof: base change of the etale map; Tag 00U2, lemma-etale, base-change assertion.

proof.text: Let $J=\mathcal D=\ker(B\to R)$. Multiplication $B\to R$ is onto, since $r\otimes1\mapsto r$, so $B/J=R$. The composite $A\to B/J$ is the surjection $e$ of Step 1 and has kernel $I=\ker e$. The etale case of [lem-sfb-augmented-etale-associated-graded] applies to exactly $\varphi,A,B,I,J$; at exponent $t+1\ge1$ it gives $A/I^{t+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}B/J^{t+1}$. By [def-trf-diagonal-jets] the latter ring is $P^t_{R/R_0}$. Combine with Step 1 to obtain the required $R$-algebra isomorphism $\Phi_t$. Its formula is $Y_j\mapsto1\otimes z_j-z_j\otimes1$, because $Y_j=X_j-z_j$ in $A$. This also identifies the displayed finite monomial basis with the corresponding coordinate-difference monomials in principal parts.

source.place: Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega, diagonal-power quotient assertion and proof via Tag 0H1D, lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal; Tag 0H90, lemma-principal-parts-diagonal.

proof.text: The map $h\mapsto1\otimes h$ followed by the quotient is an $R_0$-algebra homomorphism, so $T_t=\Phi_t^{-1}(1\otimes-)$ is one too. The formula for $\Phi_t$ gives $T_t(z_j)=z_j+Y_j$. Reducing $\Phi_t$ modulo $(Y)$ is multiplication $B\to R$, hence $T_t(h)\bmod(Y)=h$. For $s\le t$, the two maps from $R[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$ to $P^s_{R/R_0}$ obtained by truncating either side send $r\in R$ to $r\otimes1$ and $Y_j$ to the same coordinate difference. They are equal by polynomial evaluation and the quotient definition. Applying the inverse isomorphisms to $1\otimes h$ proves truncation compatibility for $T_t$ as well.

source.place: Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega, canonical quotient maps; Tag 0H90, lemma-principal-parts-diagonal, second-factor universal map.

proof.text: Fix $R_0\to R'_0$ and put $S'=R'_0[z]$, $R'=R\otimes_{R_0}R'_0$. Tensor balancing identifies $S'\otimes_SR$ with $R'$ by $f(z)\otimes r\mapsto\sum_\alpha(z^\alpha r)\otimes a_\alpha$ for $f=\sum a_\alpha z^\alpha$, with inverse $r\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes r$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] applied to $S\to R$ and $S\to S'$ makes $R'$ etale over $S'$. Steps 1--3 apply to these primed rings, giving $\Phi'_t:R'[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}\simeq P^t_{R'/R'_0}$ with the same formula for $Y_j$.

source.place: Tag 00U2, lemma-etale, base change; Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega, applied over the changed base.

proof.text: The canonical map $\theta_t:P^t_{R/R_0}\otimes_{R_0}R'_0\to P^t_{R'/R'_0}$ sends $[r\otimes u]\otimes a$ to $[(r\otimes a)\otimes_{R'_0}(u\otimes1)]$. It is well defined: the tensor balancing relations are preserved, and a diagonal-kernel element maps to a diagonal-kernel element, so products of $t+1$ such elements map to zero. The finite monomial expansion of Step 1 identifies the source, via $\Phi_t$, with $R'[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$: its map sends $(rY^\alpha)\otimes a$ to $(r\otimes a)Y^\alpha$ and its inverse sends each coefficient $(r\otimes a)Y^\alpha$ to $(rY^\alpha)\otimes a$, extended additively. These formulas are balanced and inverse on generators. Under this identification and $\Phi'_t$, $\theta_t$ fixes every coefficient in $R'$ and every $Y_j$, and is therefore the identity. This proves its bijectivity and the basis assertion without tensoring an exact sequence. Finally, $\theta_t([1\otimes h]\otimes a)$ is the class of $1\otimes(h\otimes a)$, so the maps $T_t$ after base change agree on all $h\otimes a$, which additively generate $R'$.

proof.text:
Write $E_t=C[[Z]][Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$. For $f=\sum_
u c_

u$, define its formal translation $\delta_t(f)\in E_t$ by
$$[Z^\alpha Y^ eta]\delta_t(f)= inom{\alpha+ eta}{ eta}c_{\alpha+ eta}\quad(| eta|\le t),\qquad  inom{
u}{ eta}=\prod_j inom{
u_j}{ eta_j}.$$
There are finitely many allowed $ eta$, and each displayed coefficient is one element of $C$, so this defines an element of $E_t$ over every commutative ring, including rings of positive characteristic. It fixes constant series, is additive, sends $Z_j$ to $Z_j+Y_j$, and reduces to the identity modulo $(Y)$. It is continuous: a monomial of total degree at least $q+t$ contributes only terms with $Z$-degree at least $q$, since its $Y$-degree is at most $t$. Thus $\delta_t((Z)^{q+t})\subseteq (Z)^qE_t$, which gives continuity for the coefficient-variable adic topology, and hence also for the topology generated by all variables. This is precisely the coefficientwise binomial expansion meant in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega, compatibility with a chosen power-series realization: explicit coefficientwise translation calculation supplied here.

proof.text:
The map $\delta_t$ is multiplicative, as follows directly from convolution. For $f=\sum f_uZ^u$, $g=\sum g_vZ^v$ and $|\beta|\le t$, the coefficient of $Z^\alpha Y^\beta$ in $\delta_t(f)\delta_t(g)$ is
$$\sum_{u+v=\alpha+\beta} f_ug_v\sum_{b+c=\beta,\ b\le u,\ c\le v}\binom ub\binom vc
=\binom{\alpha+\beta}{\beta}\sum_{u+v=\alpha+\beta}f_ug_v.$$
All sums are finite. The inner identity is the coefficient of $X^\beta$ in $\prod_j(1+X_j)^{u_j}(1+X_j)^{v_j}=\prod_j(1+X_j)^{u_j+v_j}$, so it holds over $\mathbf Z$ and after mapping to $C$. The last expression is the coefficient in $\delta_t(fg)$. Terms discarded modulo $(Y)^{t+1}$ cannot contribute to a coefficient with $|\beta|\le t$. Thus $\delta_t$ is a $C$-algebra homomorphism. This calculation is only the finite multiplication formula of power series and the polynomial binomial identity, not an appeal to a substitution theorem with additional hypotheses.

source.place: Coefficient calculation for the formal-translation compatibility following Tag 0H93; polynomial binomial expansion and the defining convolution product.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] applied to $S\to R$, $\Omega_{R/S}=0$. The implication (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) of [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-ring-iff-kahler-zero] therefore gives uniqueness of $S$-algebra lifts to any square-zero extension. It gives uniqueness also modulo powers of a nilpotent ideal: if two $S$-algebra maps $R\to E_t$ agree modulo $K=(Y)$, induct on $k=1,\ldots,t$. The quotient map $E_t/K^{k+1}\to E_t/K^k$ has kernel $K^k/K^{k+1}$ with square zero because $2k\ge k+1$. If the maps agree at level $k$, the cited uniqueness applied to this square-zero ideal makes them agree at level $k+1$. At $k=t+1$ the ideal power is zero. This argument compares existing maps, so no lifting existence or completeness assumption is being inserted.

source.place: Tags 00U1, definition-etale, and 00UO, lemma-characterize-formally-unramified; the successive square-zero uniqueness argument also used in Tag 0H1D.

proof.text: Now let $\tau$ be as in the statement, and apply it coefficientwise to $T_t$ to obtain $F:R\to E_t$. Polynomial evaluation makes $F$ a ring homomorphism, and $G=\delta_t\circ\tau:R\to E_t$ is another by Step 8. Give $E_t$ its $S=R_0[z]$-algebra structure by $z_j\mapsto Z_j+Y_j$ and the given map $R_0\to C$. Both $F$ and $G$ respect this structure, since $T_t(z_j)=z_j+Y_j$, $\tau(z_j)=Z_j$, and $\tau$ is an $R_0$-algebra map. Both reduce to $\tau$ modulo $(Y)$. The uniqueness proved in Step 9 gives $F=G$, which is the required identity $\tau(T_t(h))=\tau(h)(Z+Y)\bmod(Y)^{t+1}$ for every $h$. For $t=0$ this comparison is already equality modulo $(Y)=0$; for $n=0$ all polynomial and series variable sets are empty and the coordinate ring in Step 1 is $R$. All formulas and the cited lemmas allow zero rings. No factorial is inverted, no ideal of $R$ is chosen, and no flatness of a coefficient change is used.

((1 : R₀') ⊗ₜ[R₀] φ (MvPolynomial.X j)) ⊗ₜ[R₀'] (1 : R₀' ⊗[R₀] R))) ∧ (∀ (t : ℕ) (a : R₀') (r h : R), θ t (a ⊗ₜ[R₀] principalMk R₀ R t (r ⊗ₜ[R₀] h)) = principalMk R₀' (R₀' ⊗[R₀] R) t ((a ⊗ₜ[R₀] r) ⊗ₜ[R₀'] ((1 : R₀') ⊗ₜ[R₀] h))) ∧ (∀ (t : ℕ) (a : R₀') (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R), θ t (a ⊗ₜ[R₀] e t (coordinateMk R n t p)) = e' t (coordinateMk (R₀' ⊗[R₀] R) n t (MvPolynomial.C (a ⊗ₜ[R₀] (1 : R)) * MvPolynomial.map Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom p))) ∧ (∀ (t : ℕ) (a : R₀') (h : R) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R), coordinateMk R n t p = coordinateTaylor R₀ R n t (e t) h → coordinateTaylor R₀' (R₀' ⊗[R₀] R) n t (e' t) (a ⊗ₜ[R₀] h) = coordinateMk (R₀' ⊗[R₀] R) n t (MvPolynomial.C (a ⊗ₜ[R₀] (1 : R)) * MvPolynomial.map Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom p))) ∧ (∀ (C : Type x) [CommRing C] [Algebra R₀ C] (τ : R →ₐ[R₀] MvPowerSeries (Fin n) C), (∀ j : Fin n, τ (φ (MvPolynomial.X j)) = MvPowerSeries.X j) → ∀ (t : ℕ) (h : R) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R), coordinateMk R n t p = coordinateTaylor R₀ R n t (e t) h → ∀ (α β : Fin n →₀ ℕ), β.sum (fun _ k ↦ k) ≤ t → MvPowerSeries.coeff α (τ (MvPolynomial.coeff β p)) = (∏ j : Fin n, Nat.choose (α j + β j) (β j)) • MvPowerSeries.coeff (α + β) (τ h))

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause match with the node and Stacks 0H93/0H90/0H8Z. Coordinate isos e_t pinned on Y_j ↦ [1⊗z_j−z_j⊗1] (canonical). T_t = e⁻¹∘(1⊗−): T(z_j)=z_j+Y_j; mod-(Y) clause via constantCoeff of every representative. Truncation stated for e and T; monomial basis indexed by |β|≤t. Base change over any R₀' (no flatness): θ pinned on a⊗[r⊗h], e' pinned on generators; coefficient/basis and Taylor formulas checked. Formal translation coefficientwise: coeff_α τ(p_β) = ∏C(α+β,β)•coeff_{α+β}τ(h) for |β|≤t, which fixes the class mod (Y)^{t+1} by mem_pow_idealOfVars_iff'; hand example n=1, h=z², t=2 checked. Edge cases n=0, t=0, zero rings, char p checked; universes u,v,w,x independent. No duplicate: reuses DiagonalJets.principalParts and MvPolynomial.idealOfVars; JetDiagramHilbertControl (field, CharZero) and DiagonalTaylorFaithfulFlatness (residue point) are different statements.
